A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same test-time scaling study. Their full text, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, pagination, and appendix numbering.

before.justification: Sections 2–4 and Appendix C report original experiments on reasoning accuracy and response entropy, including comparisons of thinking-budget strategies. Appendix D supplies generated examples.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, including the appendix analyses and examples. Section 3.1 additionally reports a context-length control experiment on GSM-8K.

M1.justification: Parallel thinking still generates independent reasoning traces within a total token budget and selects the answer by majority vote. The existing budget-control procedures are unchanged; repeated-trace extension is introduced only as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical reasoning tasks on GSM-8K, MATH-500, and AIME 2024. The added repeated-trace experiment reuses GSM-8K to vary the reasoning procedure rather than extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 6 introduces 'Naive Extension' as a control comparator alongside 'Wait & Think more' and 'Standard Thinking.' The comparator sets in the retained parallel-thinking evaluations are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 adds a controlled evaluation using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on GSM-8K: sample one reasoning trace, append repeated copies, and measure final-answer accuracy and entropy. Existing benchmark splits, model configurations, metrics, and budget-control settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Figure 6 analysis tests whether longer context alone explains increasing response entropy by holding the repeated reasoning content fixed. The existing minimum-budget analyses, additional-model entropy analyses, and generation examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the multiple-answer sampling description is unchanged. The additional entropy curve measures response variability; it does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds results showing nearly constant accuracy and entropy under Naive Extension, compared with changing accuracy and increasing entropy under Wait & Think more. Existing numerical findings, plotted results, and appendix examples are retained without substantive changes.

T1.justification: The Gaussian policy/reward assumptions, expected-reward expression, and variance argument are unchanged. The majority-vote equation moves from displayed Equation 5 to inline text without changing its definition. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim non-monotonic performance under extended thinking, a variance-based explanation, and more effective budget use through parallel thinking. The new title and 'mirage' wording restate the existing illusion claim rather than changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds the interpretation that context length alone does not explain the observed uncertainty increase, using repeated-trace extension as supporting evidence. The stated limitations concerning model size and the lack of a formal theoretical account remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The software and hardware disclosure is unchanged: Python 3.11.11, PyTorch 2.6.0, Transformers 4.49.0, and Nvidia RTX A6000 GPUs, moved from Appendix B to D. No additional implementation hyperparameters or code/data access information accompanies the new control protocol.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. General reasoning background and the discussion of concurrent overthinking studies move from Section 5 to Appendix C. 'OpenAIo1' corrects attribution of an already cited work.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Understanding' to 'Mirage of' test-time scaling, with related terminology edits. Portions of related work move to the appendix, acknowledgments are added, and affiliation/conference text changes. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the two-panel Figure 6 with accuracy and entropy curves. Existing figures are retained but renumbered or resized; the fixed-budget bar chart becomes a smaller figure beside the method text. Appendix figures and examples are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: The added control in Section 3.1 and Figure 6 provides useful evidence against context length alone explaining rising entropy, addressing an alternative explanation left untested in v1. This strengthens the empirical argument modestly, but the experiment covers only one model and dataset and does not establish the broader causal claim. The remaining scientific content is largely unchanged.
